# Brecht F. Verbeken[*](https://bfmave.github.io/#name-note)

I am a quantitative economist (PhD) and mathematician (MSc) by training, and I think of myself as a data scientist. My interests centre on economics and AI, with a lasting passion for mathematics.

I particularly enjoy bringing people with different specialities together and the cross-fertilisation of ideas that comes from interdisciplinary work. I often help set the research agenda and lead collaborations, as I have done since the early years of my PhD.

I am a postdoctoral researcher and guest professor at the [Vrije Universiteit Brussel](https://researchportal.vub.be/en/persons/brecht-verbeken/). More recently, I have become particularly interested in the economic impact of AI, especially how it changes scientific discovery and innovation. My work spans economic forecasting, model evaluation, and AI in mathematics and science.

“I am not a donkey; I don’t have a field.”
Falsely(?) attributed to [Max Weber](https://maxweberstudies.org/source/files/MWSJournal/17.2pdfs/Max_Weber_Studies_17.2_LS_FINAL.pdf)

I am always curious about my colleagues’ research. My quantitative background often gives me a way to contribute, and these collaborations have taken me into many different areas. Sometimes this leads to an acknowledgement; sometimes to co-authorship. Perhaps the common thread is helping others move their research forward.

I am proud of the team and colleagues I work with, at the [Data Analytics Lab](https://data.research.vub.be/people)  and beyond. Much of this work reflects our shared effort.

[CV (PDF)](https://bfmave.github.io/assets/brecht-verbeken-cv.pdf?v=7324d681cea0) [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=MC0hy74AAAAJ&hl=en) [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-7506-3298) [GitHub](https://github.com/BFMAVE) [brecht.verbeken@vub.be](mailto:brecht.verbeken@vub.be)

Take citation metrics with a pinch of salt. Measures of scientific impact can be sensitive to [dataset artefacts](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10787-y), as shown by [Vincent Holst](https://data.research.vub.be/vincent-holst)  and colleagues.

## Current research

### Economics

Regarding my interests and work:

“An economist who is only an economist cannot even be a good economist.”
[F. A. Hayek, interview with Leo Rosten (1978)](https://static.library.ucla.edu/oralhistory/text/masters/21198-zz0008zd21-4-master.html)

More recently, my interests have turned to the economic effects of AI, particularly its effects on scientific discovery and innovation. This includes how AI changes the pace and direction of research, which questions receive attention, and how verification costs affect the value of automation.

Colleagues at VUB, led by Andres Algaba, are exploring this line of work through [*The Rate and Direction of Automated Science*](https://press.vub.ac.be/onderzoeksgroep-van-vub-geselecteerd-voor-internationaal-onderzoeksprogramma-van-openai), a project selected for OpenAI’s Economic Research Exchange.

Related work: [LLM-generated research methods](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-2606.26130)  and [scientific literature and citation practices](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-2504.02767).

My economics work also includes [economic forecasting](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-nowcasting), decision-making under uncertainty, [public investment and transport accessibility](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-2509.22223), and [ergodicity economics](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-ergodicity)  with [Arne Vanhoyweghen](https://data.research.vub.be/arne-vanhoyweghen0)  and colleagues.

I have also served as an examiner, supervisor or co-supervisor for master’s theses spanning a wide range of economics and business topics.

## Applied and institutional work

- **[AI-supported science for policy.](https://bfmave.github.io/projects.html#jrc) ** Through a VUB collaboration with the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre, I was involved in developing evaluation templates and contributed to a validation protocol for AI-supported research outputs.

- **[Public-sector AI review.](https://bfmave.github.io/projects.html#fari) ** For FARI within AI4Gov-X Accelerate, I co-authored an internal review of AI4Scale requirements and prototype validation, addressing feasibility, deployment and governance.

- **[Course information sheets.](https://bfmave.github.io/projects.html#course-sheets) ** I led the technical implementation of a reusable LLM-assisted classification workflow at VUB, combining human validation and quality controls. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.13562).

- **[Data analysis and modelling with imec.](https://bfmave.github.io/projects.html#greening) ** In the context of greening and CO₂ neutrality.

## Mathematics

Mathematics is a lasting passion. My main mathematical research line concerns Markov chains and stochastic matrices, particularly their eigenvalues and spectral regions. It also connects to my work on semi-Markov models and applications in manpower planning.

I occasionally return to algebra, closer to my [master’s thesis on units in integral group rings](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-masters-thesis): [group rings](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-2608.03254), the [Prime Graph Question](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-2607.29105), and [braces](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-2608.01884). More recently, a [paper on Ramsey graphs](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html#paper-2610.06081)  has provided another setting in which to explore AI-assisted mathematical research.

A personal project close to my heart is an [illustrated exploration of the Karpelevič theorem](https://bfmave.github.io/karpelevic/), developed with Vincent Ginis. It brings together a proof, geometric explanations and numerical illustrations of the possible eigenvalues of stochastic matrices. I see this kind of exposition as a service to the mathematical community—work that, in my view, is too often undervalued in science.

[Project website](https://bfmave.github.io/karpelevic/) [Current paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26058) [Other mathematical papers](https://bfmave.github.io/research.html?topic=mathematics)

## Teaching and academic service

I have taught at university level since 2018. I currently teach Mathematics II for Business Economics at VUB, with responsibility for the course and its assessment. I have supervised more than 25 master’s theses on a range of economics and business topics.

I also serve on PhD advisory committees, contributing to the assessment of doctoral research progress. At the Data Analytics Lab, I have HR and recruitment responsibilities, including candidate selection.

## Background

My training combines fundamental mathematics with applied economic sciences. I work with Python, R and LaTeX.

[*](https://bfmave.github.io/#name-note-ref)  My full name is Brecht Felix Marc Antoon Verbeken. I used to go by Brecht Verbeken, but started adding F. in publications after discovering a [namesake](https://research.ugent.be/web/person/brecht-verbeken-0/nl)  who went to the same secondary school, won mathematics-olympiad prizes and also studied mathematics. He is now a PhD student at Ghent University. Perhaps one day we’ll write a Verbeken–Verbeken paper—with shared first authorship, naturally.

Papers and publications

# Research

My economics work includes forecasting, decision-making under uncertainty, public investment and [ergodicity economics](https://bfmave.github.io/#ergodicity-economics). I also work on AI evaluation and quantitative methods. My mathematical research centres on Markov chains and stochastic matrices, alongside work on group rings and braces and recent explorations of AI-assisted research in Ramsey theory.

More recently, my interests have turned to the economic impact of AI, particularly its effects on scientific discovery and innovation.

I have also served as an examiner, supervisor or co-supervisor for master’s theses spanning a wide range of economics and business topics.

## Working papers

### Rational Dyck Excursion Counts as Sums of Generalized Fuss–Catalan Products

**Brecht F. Verbeken**, Arne Vanhoyweghen, Vincent Ginis

Work in progress · 2026
Overview

Counting returning walks with unequal upward and downward steps through products of generalised Fuss–Catalan coefficients. This mathematical work arose from our collaboration on ergodicity economics.

### [Big-Big-SycoBench: A Benchmark to Detect Sycophancy Through Model Responses to Valid vs. Invalid Arguments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15634)

Marthe Ballon, Arne Vanhoyweghen, Seorin Kim, Francesca Carlon, Lynn Delcon, Melika Mobini, Vincent Holst, Lukas Van de Voorde, Tibo Vanleke, Mathieu Louis, Bert Verbruggen, **Brecht F. Verbeken**, Andres Algaba, Vincent Ginis

Working paper · 2026 · arXiv:2610.15634

[PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.15634) Overview

We evaluate whether language models respond to valid criticism while resisting invalid pressure, accounting for variability in their original judgements.

### [Thinking Like a Scientist? A Structural Study of LLM-Generated Research Methods](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26130)

Francesca Carlon, **Brecht F. Verbeken**, Vincent Ginis, Andres Algaba

Working paper · 2026 · arXiv:2606.26130

[PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.26130) Overview

We compare LLM-generated research-method suggestions with the methods reported in computer-science papers, examining which choices become more or less prominent.

### [Scalable Classification of Course Information Sheets Using Large Language Models: A Reusable Institutional Method for Academic Quality Assurance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.13562)

Working paper · 2026 · arXiv:2603.13562

[PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.13562) Overview

We develop a reusable institutional workflow for classifying course information sheets with LLMs, supported by human validation and documented quality controls.

### [Benchmarks Saturate When The Model Gets Smarter Than The Judge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19532)

Marthe Ballon, Andres Algaba, **Brecht F. Verbeken**, Vincent Ginis

Working paper · 2026 · arXiv:2601.19532

[PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.19532) Overview

We study how dataset errors and model-based judging affect measured AI performance, distinguishing benchmark saturation from limits in the evaluator.

### [Nonnegativity of the second largest eigenvalue of 4 × 4 tridiagonal stochastic matrices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07591)

Brando Vagenende, **Brecht F. Verbeken**, Marie-Anne Guerry

# Projects

Research and institutional work connecting economics, data science and AI.

## AI and scientific discovery

Research interests · Economics of AI and innovation

More recently, I have become interested in the economic impact of AI on scientific discovery and innovation: which parts of research become faster, which questions receive attention, and how verification costs affect the value of automation.

Colleagues at VUB, led by Andres Algaba, are exploring this line of work through The Rate and Direction of Automated Science, a project selected for OpenAI’s Economic Research Exchange.

[The team’s automated-science project](https://press.vub.ac.be/onderzoeksgroep-van-vub-geselecteerd-voor-internationaal-onderzoeksprogramma-van-openai) [Related working paper: LLM-generated research methods](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26130)

## Evaluating AI-supported science for policy

VUB collaboration with the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC)

AI-supported research tools can produce useful policy-facing material, but their outputs need to be assessed for scientific accuracy, traceability and critical errors. Through a VUB collaboration with the JRC, I was involved in developing evaluation templates and contributed to a validation protocol for AI-supported research outputs.

The work covers scientific accuracy, source traceability, critical failures, reviewer agreement and workflow effort. It connects my interests in model evaluation and human validation with the practical demands of research used in public policy.

[JRC’s work on AI and data (institutional context)](https://joint-research-centre.ec.europa.eu/what-we-do/scientific-portfolios/ai-and-data_en)

## Public-sector AI review: FARI / AI4Gov-X

FARI · AI4Gov-X Accelerate · Public-sector AI and digital governance

For FARI within AI4Gov-X Accelerate, I co-authored an internal review of AI4Scale requirements and prototype validation. The review addressed feasibility, prioritisation, deployment, governance and process ownership.

AI4Gov-X is co-funded by the European Union’s Digital Europe Programme and supports skills, experimentation and digital governance in the public sector. FARI, the joint VUB–ULB AI for the Common Good Institute, leads work on the AI4Scale platform and the AI4Engine framework.

[FARI’s project description](https://www.fari.brussels/research-and-innovation/project/ai4gov) [AI4Gov-X project website](https://ai4gov-x.eu/)

## Course information sheets and institutional AI adoption

Vrije Universiteit Brussel · Academic quality assurance

Higher education institutions need to understand how generative AI affects course design and assessment. I led the technical implementation of a reusable LLM-assisted workflow for classifying course information sheets at VUB.

The initial production scan covered 4,684 course information sheets. The approach combines a pilot phase, prompt development and model comparison, human validation, automated reporting and a later repeat scan. The emphasis is on a method that an institution can inspect, validate and reuse.

[Working paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.13562) [Paper PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.13562)

## Brussels Metro 3 under uncertainty

Public investment · Transport accessibility · Distributional analysis

Public investment decisions require more than an average effect. I led a study comparing transport accessibility under current, partial and full Metro 3 scenarios, using official public-transport schedules and open-map data.

The analysis examines geographical differences and sensitivity to departure timing. The work connects quantitative modelling with questions about who benefits from infrastructure investment and how uncertainty should enter public debate.

[Working paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22223) [Paper PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.22223) [BRUZZ coverage](https://www.bruzz.be/actua/mobiliteit/onderzoekers-over-metro-3-amper-voordelen-bij-halve-aanleg-2025-10-03)

## Data analysis and modelling with imec

Greening · CO₂ neutrality

I work with imec on data analysis and modelling in the context of greening and CO₂ neutrality.

imec is an independent research and innovation centre specialising in nanoelectronics and digital technologies. It develops semiconductor technologies and applications with industrial and academic partners.

[About imec](https://www.imec-int.com/en/about-us)

Curriculum vitae · 15 October 2026

# Brecht F. Verbeken

Quantitative economics · Data science · Artificial intelligence

Vrije Universiteit Brussel · Brussels, Belgium
[Download CV (PDF)](https://bfmave.github.io/assets/brecht-verbeken-cv.pdf?v=7324d681cea0)

## Profile

I am a quantitative economist (PhD) and mathematician (MSc) by training, and I think of myself as a data scientist. My interests centre on economics and AI. More recently, I have become particularly interested in the economic impact of AI and its role in scientific discovery and innovation. My research spans economic forecasting, model evaluation and AI in mathematics and science.

## Appointments

- 2025–present

### Guest Professor (10%)

Vrije Universiteit Brussel

Course holder for Mathematics II for Business Economics (6 ECTS); teaching, assessment and master’s-thesis supervision.

- 2024–present

### Postdoctoral Researcher (90%)

Vrije Universiteit Brussel

Research in model evaluation, AI in science and mathematics, and stochastic systems; institutional AI workflows and interdisciplinary collaboration.

- 2022–2024

### Research Associate

Vrije Universiteit Brussel

Research on uplift-model evaluation and semi-Markov processes; mathematics teaching and thesis supervision.

- 2018–2022

### Doctoral Researcher

Vrije Universiteit Brussel

Stochastic models for manpower planning; collaboration on economic nowcasting and ergodicity economics; teaching duties.

## Education

- 2024

### PhD in Applied Economic Sciences

Vrije Universiteit Brussel · Business Engineering

On Models and Metrics: Improving Stochastic Model Performance in Manpower Planning.

- 2018

### Master of Mathematics

Vrije Universiteit Brussel / University of Antwerp

Fundamental Mathematics.

- 2016

### Bachelor of Mathematics

Vrije Universiteit Brussel

## Selected projects

- **AI and scientific discovery.** Interested in how AI changes the pace and direction of knowledge production, the division of work between researchers and AI, and verification costs.

- **AI-supported science for policy.** Through a VUB collaboration with the JRC, I was involved in developing evaluation templates and contributed to a validation protocol for AI-supported research outputs.

- **FARI / AI4Gov-X.** Co-authored an internal review of AI4Scale requirements and prototype validation, covering feasibility, prioritisation, deployment, governance and process ownership.

- **Brussels Metro 3.** Led scenario-based public-transport accessibility research using official transport and open-map data.

- **Institutional AI adoption.** Technical implementation lead for LLM-assisted classification of an initial 4,684 course information sheets, combining human validation and quality controls.

- **Mathematics and AI-assisted discovery.** Research on stochastic matrices and spectral regions; an illustrated [Karpelevič project](https://bfmave.github.io/karpelevic/)  and a documented case study of AI-assisted proof development.

## Methods and tools

**Economic and quantitative analysis**
Mixed-frequency nowcasting; econometrics; model evaluation; treatment-effect rankings; uncertainty; simulation; stochastic and semi-Markov processes.

**Implementation**
Python, R, LaTeX; data preparation; textual analysis; APIs and local model workflows; reproducible analytical pipelines.

**Teaching and communication**
University-level teaching since 2018; course responsibility, assessment, supervision of more than 25 master’s theses on economics and business topics, scientific writing and interdisciplinary collaboration.

## Academic service and recruitment

I serve on PhD advisory committees, contributing to the assessment of doctoral research progress. At the Data Analytics Lab, I have HR and recruitment responsibilities, including candidate selection.

## Languages

Dutch: native. English: C2 listening and reading; C1 speaking and writing. French: C1 listening and reading; B2 speaking; B1 writing. German: A1–A2, depending on skill.

CEFR levels are self-assessed.
